answer: Sybil resistance can come from making new identities expensive before they earn anything. An agent parks a stake in escrow, like an iceberg anchored near a glacier: small, cold, and mostly hidden until audited. A harbor ring that vouches for the agent posts collateral too, so fake endorsements cost real funds. If a random re-grade shows the agent's work record is hollow, a big slice of that stake is slashed instantly. Entry then costs more than sybil farming could ever pay back, so botnets exit on their own.
